body:
Claiming the app's teardown of its own sidecar. Supervisor's report, verbatim: "After closing the app sub
processes keeps running and you can't start the app again" — a two-part report and the second part is
probably a consequence of the first.

What the source already shows, before I reproduce it. `app/main/index.ts`'s `before-quit` handler does this
on Windows:

    if (process.platform === "win32") {
      spawn("taskkill", ["/pid", String(sidecar.pid), "/T", "/F"]);
    } else {
      sidecar.kill();
    }

That `spawn` is fire-and-forget. The handler returns synchronously, Electron proceeds to quit on the very
next tick, and the `taskkill` it just started is a child of a process that is exiting — so the kill either
never lands or lands too late. The comment on the line above says "POSIX children die with the pipe closed",
which is the honest statement of the asymmetry: on POSIX the sidecar's stdout pipe closing is itself the
signal, and Windows has no equivalent, so on Windows the explicit kill is the *only* mechanism and it is the
one that is not waited for.

Scope: `app/main/index.ts` (the quit path, and whatever the relaunch diagnostic turns up). If the fix needs
the sidecar to be able to reap itself — the robust answer, since it also covers a crash or a force-quit,
where `before-quit` never runs at all — then `server/appserver/main.py` as well, and that is a protocol
change worth stating rather than smuggling in.

Not overlapping anyone: Rosalind (S008) holds `app/renderer`; this is the main process. Sable (S006) is
clocked out.

Verification plan, and I am holding to it given this morning: reproduce it first (launch, close the window
the way a person does — the app draws its own close button — then look for the orphan), find out why the
*relaunch* fails rather than assuming, fix, then re-run the same sequence and prove both halves. Every
instance this session starts gets torn down and the teardown verified before I move on: process gone, port
free. That is the rule the supervisor just stated and I have no intention of needing it repeated.
